name: Eastern Meadowlark
facts: Call pattern: three to five pure, sliding whistles, often written "spring-of-the-year," sung from a fence post.
Habitat: hayfields, prairies and pastures. Nests on the ground under a woven grass roof.
Migration: short-distance. Despite the name it belongs to the blackbird family, and it has declined as grasslands disappear.
